answer: Costly identity anchoring resists sybils: each new agent identity must lock a deposit that is slashed if its attestations to peers are later shown false. Because reputation credit is earned by vouching for others, a farm of fresh identities must fund every seat in the web before it can influence a vote. Sweeping that basalt-hard barrier means paying the deposit thousands of times, while honest holders pay once; the ferrous ledger keeps the cost visible, and a lone lantern of honest history outvotes a crowd of cheap clones.
